clue.text: Casual way to feed tame bird?

definitions.meaning: an ... remark is casual or careless
a tame bird will take food straight from your palm, eaten off the hand

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: careless in manner, and the literal phrase for eating from a person's palm.

clue.text: Light-hearted, though initially deprived of sight

indicators.note: initially deprived means losing the first letter

parts.note: jocular means joking, light-hearted

explanation.surface: Cheerful despite going blind.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocular means relating to the eye, so to do with seeing.

clue.text: St Peter's edict covering woman

indicators.note: covering means the edict wraps around the woman

parts.note: a firman is an edict issued by an Eastern ruler
she stands for a woman

explanation.surface: A saint's decree that protects a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the 's as 'is'. FIRMAN, a sultan's decree, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter was a Galilean who caught fish before becoming an apostle.

clue.text: American city's impressive area

parts.note: august means grand and impressive

explanation.surface: A US city boasting a grand region.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is the capital of Maine and a city in Georgia, home of the Masters golf.

clue.text: Computer-controlled stores of fruit, about a half of basket

indicators.note: about means the fruit goes around the rest

parts.note: dates are a fruit

indicators.note: a half of picks the first three letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Shops selling fruit by the half-basket.
explanation.definitionFit: Databases are organised stores of information held on computers.

clue.text: Renovate coat by mistake

parts.note: an animal's coat is its fur
bish is British slang for a blunder

explanation.surface: Someone does up an old coat and gets it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: BISH is informal British slang for a mistake; 'by' just sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To furbish something is to polish it up or restore it, the same as renovating it.

clue.text: In favour of keeping the old hall

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside

parts.note: for means in favour of
ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: Supporting preservation of an old hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A foyer is an entrance hall in a theatre or hotel.

clue.text: Books I hurry round to criticise

indicators.note: round means the hurry word goes around the others

parts.note: to rush is to hurry
BB is short for books, B doubled

explanation.surface: A hasty review panning some books.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubbish something is to disparage it, informal British usage.

clue.text: Wordsworth's boy, one I introduced to his sister briefly

parts.note: the Roman numeral one is I

indicators.note: introduced to means put inside

parts.note: Wordsworth's sister was Dorothy, shortened to Dot

explanation.surface: Wordsworth presenting a friend to his sister.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth wrote 'The Idiot Boy'; his sister was Dorothy.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's title character is a simple-minded boy, Johnny.

clue.text: Sort of block substantial pay increase

parts.note: high means large, as in a high price
a rise is the British word for a pay increase

explanation.surface: A whopping salary hike.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'rise' is British for what Americans call a raise.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower block of many storeys is called high-rise.

clue.text: Like dreadfully ugly things, less good?

definitions.text: Like dreadfully ugly things, less good?

indicators.note: dreadfully says the letters of the words before it are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A wry question whether ugly things are simply worse.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of UGLY THINGS, remove G ('less good'), and rearrange the rest; the whole clue also describes the answer, since ugly things are unsightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly things are unpleasant to look at, which is exactly what unsightly describes.

clue.text: Provide bachelor with token of love

parts.note: a ring is given as a token of love

explanation.surface: Giving a single man an engagement ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something is to supply or provide it.

clue.text: Resemble, in parts

definitions.meaning: read as two words, '...' means to be like, to resemble
regions or districts, as in 'parts of the country'

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the letters say 'are as', meaning look like; whole, they mean regions or districts.

clue.text: Lawyer is pursuing right to be in trade

indicators.note: to be in tells us the pair goes inside the trade word

parts.note: to barter is to trade goods

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so is follows right

explanation.surface: A lawyer chasing his rights in commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister is a lawyer who argues cases in the higher courts in Britain.

clue.text: Fare on vehicle specially fixed for the elderly?

definitions.text: Fare on vehicle specially fixed for the elderly?

parts.words: Fare on vehicle specially fixed for the elderly?
parts.note: fare is food, a vehicle is a thing on wheels, and the service is arranged for old people who cannot cook

explanation.definitionFit: The service delivers hot food by van to elderly or housebound people, literally food on wheels.

clue.text: Edward infested? Don't worry

annotationWithheld.why: Edward infested? Don't worry: NED around VERMIN, but 'infested' must be both the container signal and the source of VERMIN, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Joy about even 50% getting promotion

indicators.note: about says the joy word goes around the half

parts.note: elation is great joy

indicators.note: 50% picks half, the first two letters

explanation.surface: Delight at getting an even half of a raise and a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevation means raising to a higher rank.

clue.text: Final set of questions — one's stuck, quite blank

parts.note: end means final part
an exam paper is a set of questions

explanation.surface: A student stuck on the final exam, mind blank.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about exam panic; the definition describes the plain sheet glued inside a book's cover.
explanation.definitionFit: An endpaper is the blank leaf pasted to the inside of a book's binding.

clue.text: Lines for the Fool in production of Lear?

definitions.text: Lines for the Fool in production of Lear?

parts.words: Lines for the Fool in production of Lear?
parts.note: reads as the script for the Fool in a staging of King Lear, but Edward Lear produced silly rhymes

explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's King Lear has a Fool with riddling lines, but the other Lear is Edward Lear, the Victorian poet of comic rhymes like The Owl and the Pussycat.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear is famous for absurd comic poems, the kind of lines a fool might speak.

clue.text: I fall in vain pursuit

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, the self
to trip is to stumble or fall

explanation.surface: Someone confessing to tumbling while chasing a futile goal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity pursued out of vanity.

clue.text: Liqueur or rum at a fair

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Choosing drinks at a fairground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like another drink but is the old British adjective for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratafia is an almond-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: Dog running wild in street

indicators.note: running wild means out of order, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A stray dog loose in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a breed of gun dog.

clue.text: Exercise — it's repeated in a nasty fog

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise at school

indicators.note: in places the repeat inside the following words

parts.note: sour means unpleasant or nasty
the same exercise abbreviation appears a second time

explanation.surface: Doing exercises over and over in a thick, horrid fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' points back to the exercise, so the same letters appear twice. A pea-souper is an old British name for the thick yellow smogs of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea-souper is a dense, murky fog, named for its likeness to thick pea soup.

clue.text: Pointless court case is to cause scandal

indicators.note: pointless means missing a compass point, here East

parts.note: an appeal is a case heard by a higher court

explanation.surface: A futile lawsuit causing outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to shock or outrage people.

clue.text: They take position, accepting sheriff's lead

indicators.note: accepting means taking something inside

parts.note: to pose is to take up a position

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Lawmen getting into position under the sheriff's leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a group of people, so they refers to the members.

clue.text: Crockery one piece short? It's not serious

indicators.note: one piece short means the set is missing an item, here its final letter

parts.note: a tea set is a set of crockery

explanation.surface: Someone joking that the china set is incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: A tease is a playful taunt or joke, something not meant seriously.

clue.text: Musician Doolittle got news from?

definitions.meaning: one who plays the pipes or bagpipes
the doctor who talked to animals heard news from birds, and a young pigeon is called by this name

explanation.walkthrough: A little-known sense: a young pigeon is a piper, and the animal-loving Doctor Dolittle got messages carried by birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagpipe player is a musician; a fledgling pigeon also bears the name.

clue.text: Stone originally fell near one

indicators.note: originally says the fell word comes at the start, ahead of the stone

parts.note: a fell is an animal's hide or skin
flint is a hard stone

explanation.surface: A rock that once dropped close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a verb but is the old noun for a hide; 'near' is the dialect word for stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Near can mean mean with money, so a near one is a miser.

clue.text: Return of disease in fruit-tree I cut back

indicators.note: back says the remaining letters run in reverse
cut means the I is removed from the tree

parts.note: an espalier is a fruit tree trained flat against a wall

explanation.surface: A tree disease coming back after pruning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes I from ESPALIER to give ESPALER, and 'back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is the recurrence of an illness after apparent recovery.

clue.text: One exhausting feature of kitchen

definitions.meaning: one that empties or wears out something
a rack or board where washed dishes drip dry

explanation.definitionFit: Something that empties or tires out drains; a dish rack by the sink is also so named.
